info.title: Replica API
info.description: The Replica API allows you to programmatically manage cloud workspaces for AI agents. Use this API to manage environments (the org-scoped primitive workspaces are created from — including variables, files, skills, MCPs, warm hooks, start hooks, and warm pools), create and manage replicas, send messages, manage chats, stream events, read connected repositories and repository sets, and configure automations.

tags.name: Environments
tags.description: Manage environments — the primitive that workspaces are created from. Variables, files, skills, MCPs, warm-hooks, and warm-pools are all scoped to an environment. Every organization has a singleton Global environment whose values apply to every workspace. Personal environments are scoped to the authenticated user and can be standalone or source-backed by a team environment.

tags.name: Repository
tags.description: Read repositories and repository sets connected to your organization. Repositories are the underlying GitHub-connection layer; bind them to an environment to use them in workspaces.

tags.name: Terminal
tags.description: Manage interactive terminal sessions in active workspaces

tags.name: Preview
tags.description: Manage public preview URLs for workspace ports

tags.name: Profile
tags.description: Read and update the authenticated user's profile

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description: Manage coding-agent credentials for an organization or the authenticated user

tags.name: Google Search Console
tags.description: Read Search Console properties, performance, sitemaps, and URL inspection results through a connected Google account

tags.name: Slack
tags.description: Route Slack threads to Replicas workspaces

tags.name: Automation
tags.description: Create and manage automations that trigger replicas on a schedule or in response to events

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Read aggregated activity and usage metrics for your organization: compute minutes, workspaces created by source, and pull request throughput over a time range.

get.description: Returns environments visible to the caller, including the singleton Global environment for org scope. Each record includes counts of attached variables, files, skills, and MCPs.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by environment scope. `org` returns team environments, `user` returns your personal environments, `all` returns both. Defaults to `org`.

post.description: Creates a new team or personal environment. `repository_id` and `repository_set_id` are mutually exclusive; both may be omitted for an unbound environment that can back repo-less workspaces. Personal environments are visible only to the authenticated user. When `scope=user` and `source_environment_id` references a team environment, the personal environment inherits from that source instead of copying it.

409.description: An environment with this name already exists

get.description: Returns a single environment. Pass the literal string `global` for the org's singleton Global environment (auto-created on first access — no need to look up its UUID first).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global` for the org's Global environment.

patch.description: Updates a non-global environment. Only provided fields are changed. `PATCH /v1/environments/global` returns 400 with a pointer to the nested resource endpoints (variables, files, skills, MCPs, warm hooks) — the Global env's metadata cannot be edited directly. Source-backed personal environments cannot change `repository_id`, `repository_set_id`, or `system_prompt`, but may set `personal_preferences`, instructions appended after the inherited system prompt. Returns 409 when an automation still references the environment in a way that blocks the requested change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment UUID. The literal `global` is rejected with 400 — see endpoint description.

delete.description: Deletes an environment. Returns 409 when an automation still references the environment, when personal environments inherit from it, or when called against the Global environment (which cannot be deleted).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment UUID. The literal `global` is rejected with 409 — the Global env cannot be deleted.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

post.description: Saves the supplied script as the active warm hook for the environment and runs it in an isolated sandbox. Always persists the new version; the response includes the test result so callers can decide whether to roll back. The endpoint takes 30–90 seconds to return because it spins up a real sandbox.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

201.description: Warm hook saved (test result included in body)

post.description: Runs the supplied script in an isolated sandbox without persisting it. Useful for iterating on a warm hook from the API before committing it via `save-test`. Takes 30–90 seconds to return.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

get.description: Returns the active start hook (if any) for the environment. Start hooks run at workspace boot, after the warm sandbox is claimed; the env-level hook runs before any repository-level start hooks defined in `replicas.json` / `replicas.yaml`.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

post.description: Persists and activates the supplied script as the start hook for the environment. Empty content clears the active start hook. Editing a start hook does not invalidate the warm pool — the new content is picked up automatically on the next claim, since start hooks run at workspace boot rather than during warming.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

201.description: Start hook saved and activated, or cleared when content is empty

post.description: Runs the supplied start hook script in an isolated sandbox without persisting it, and returns the full result once the hook finishes. Useful for short-lived clients (CLI, scripts) that prefer a single response over an SSE stream. Takes 30–90 seconds to return.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

post.description: Provisions an isolated sandbox, runs the supplied start hook script, and streams output back as Server-Sent Events. Use this instead of a synchronous test endpoint to avoid gateway timeouts on long-running hooks. Events emitted: `progress` (status messages), `output` (captured stdout/stderr), `complete` (final `exit_code` and `timed_out`), and `error` (terminal failure).

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

200.description: SSE stream of start hook test events

schema.description: SSE events. Each event has `type` in {`progress`, `output`, `complete`, `error`} plus an optional `message`, `output`, `exit_code`, or `timed_out` payload.

put.description: Enables or disables the warm pool for the environment. The target pool size is fixed by the platform; only `enabled` is configurable from the API.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment UUID, or the literal string `global`.

get.description: Returns the most recent pre-warmed workspaces for a warm pool config, including their status (warming, snapshotting, ready, assigned, expired, failed). Useful for inspecting why a pool is not delivering ready workspaces. Returns up to 10 entries. To watch warm-hook output live during the `warming` phase, subscribe to [GET /v1/warm-pool-workspaces/{workspaceId}/stream](#tag/Environments/operation/streamWarmPoolWorkspace).

parameters.name: configId
parameters.description: Warm pool config UUID (from the `warm_pool.id` returned by GET `/v1/environments/{environmentId}/warm-hooks` or PUT `/v1/environments/{environmentId}/warm-pools`).

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream that delivers live warm-hook stdout/stderr plus status transitions for a single warm pool workspace. The monolith proxies output from the warming sandbox's engine; output is only available while the sandbox is running (i.e. `status` is `warming`). Once the workspace reaches `snapshotting` the sandbox is suspended and the stream stops emitting `output` events — only status transitions and the terminal `complete` event still flow. The stream auto-closes on terminal status (`ready`, `failed`, `expired`, `assigned`). Events emitted: `output` (appended chunk), `status` (transition between `warming` and `snapshotting`), `complete` (terminal with final workspace record), and `error`.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: Warm pool workspace UUID (from the `id` field returned by [GET /v1/warm-pools/{configId}/workspaces](#tag/Environments/operation/listWarmPoolWorkspaces)).

200.description: SSE stream of warm pool workspace updates

schema.description: SSE events. Each event has `type` in {`output`, `status`, `complete`, `error`} plus an optional `output`, `status`, `workspace`, or `message` payload.

See the [API Versioning](/features/api#api-versioning) section for details.

get.description: Lists the items in the replica's Canvas (files agents drop into `~/.replicas/canvas/`). Each item has a `kind` (markdown, html, image, video, audio, or other) inferred from its extension and a `sizeBytes` measured at list time. Files larger than 5 MB are still listed; the `getReplicaCanvasItem` endpoint will return `tooLarge: true` for them so callers know to fall back to `replicas media upload`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

get.description: Reads a single Canvas item by filename. Text kinds (`markdown`, `html`) return UTF-8 text in `content`. Binary kinds (`image`, `video`, `audio`, `other`) return base64 in `base64`. Items over the 5 MB per-file cap return `tooLarge: true` with neither payload; callers should reach for `replicas media upload` for those.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The Canvas item filename, including extension (e.g. `example-plan.md`).

get.description:
Opens a Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for real-time events from a replica. The connection remains open and events are pushed as they occur.

Each event is delivered as an SSE message in the format `data: <JSON>\n\n`. A heartbeat ping is sent every 15 seconds to keep the connection alive. Clients should reconnect automatically on disconnect.

All events share a common envelope structure with `id` (unique event ID), `ts` (ISO 8601 timestamp), `type` (event type discriminator), and `payload` (type-specific data). See the `EngineEvent` schema for all possible event types.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

200.description: SSE event stream opened successfully. Each line is a JSON-encoded `EngineEvent`.

post.description: Fires an automation that has a `custom` webhook trigger. The token in the URL is the secret: any caller that knows the URL can fire the automation, so this endpoint is unauthenticated by design (no API key). The request body is parsed as JSON and embedded into the automation's prompt under `## Trigger Payload`. Non-JSON bodies are wrapped as `{ "raw": "<body>" }`. Bodies larger than 256KB are rejected. Returns `202 Accepted` once the execution is queued; disabled automations, unknown tokens, and automations without a custom trigger all return `404` without distinguishing between the three.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The automation's `webhook_token`. Treat this like an API key.

schema.description: Any JSON value. The full body is embedded into the automation's prompt.

model.description: Model to use for the coding agent. Pi and Opencode accept z-ai/glm-5.2, minimax/minimax-m3, xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro, and moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 through OpenRouter.

Falls back to provider default when omitted (Claude default: high, Codex default: medium, Cursor default: medium, Opencode default: medium, Pi default: model default).

webhook_url.description: Callback target for `replica.ready`, `replica.turn_completed`, `replica.deleted`, and `replica.error` events. `replica.deleted` fires only on explicit deletion; closing a linked PR or issue now archives the workspace silently, so automated cleanup no longer emits it. `replica.error` is emitted when the workspace enters `error` state and remains queryable; the payload includes the failure message. Some wake/resume errors can be retried with the wake endpoint. Pass a bare URL string or `{ url, secret }`; with a secret the platform sets `X-Replicas-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC>` on every delivery.

size.description: Compute size for this replica. `small` (2 vCPU, 8 GB memory, 20 GB disk) bills at $0.008/min; `large` (4 vCPU, 16 GB memory, 32 GB disk) bills at $0.016/min. Defaults to `small` when omitted.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint the platform POSTs JSON events to.

secret.description: Optional shared secret used to compute the `X-Replicas-Signature` header (`sha256=` HMAC of the raw JSON body).

total.description: Total number of replicas matching the filters

success.description: Whether the sleep request was accepted

generation.description: Client generation used to reset input ordering.

sequence.description: Zero-based batch sequence within the generation.

mimeType.description: MIME type to render the content with (e.g. `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, `image/png`).

tooLarge.description: Present and `true` when the file exceeded the engine's per-file size cap.

EngineStatusSnapshot.description: A snapshot of the engine's current status

WorkspaceEngineHeartbeatSnapshot.description: Latest outbound heartbeat received from the workspace engine.

lastSeenAt.description: When the latest heartbeat was received, or null if none has been received.

ageMs.description: Age of the latest heartbeat in milliseconds, or null if none has been received.

fresh.description: Whether the latest heartbeat is within the freshness window.

bootTimeMs.description: Engine boot timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds, if reported.

uptimeSeconds.description: Engine uptime in seconds, if reported.

error.description: Status, health-check, setup/provisioning, or wake/resume error message, if present. Some workspaces in `error` can be retried with the wake endpoint; unrecoverable setup or sandbox failures may still require support.

desktopReady.description: Whether the sandbox's noVNC desktop port is accepting connections. The desktop stack boots after wake, so this can lag behind `active` status. Absent on older engines that do not report it.

repoStatuses.description: Cached repository status summaries, if available.

text.description: Preview of the most recent input message.

lastChatMessage.description: The most recent input message across the workspace's chats, or null if none has been sent.

prUrls.description: All pull request URLs the workspace has opened in this repository. A single workspace may have multiple PRs in the same repo (e.g. after switching branches or opening follow-up PRs), so this is an array. Empty when no PRs have been observed.

startHooksCompleted.description: Whether start hooks have finished executing

provider.description: Code host for the repository's origin remote, when resolvable

EngineRepoDiff.description: Git diff statistics for a repository

EngineChatSummary.description: Summary of a chat session as reported by the engine

updatedAt.description: When the chat was last updated

processing.description: Whether the chat is currently doing work — either processing a foreground message or running background/spawned-agent tasks

awaitingInput.description: The agent has issued an interactive tool call (e.g. ExitPlanMode, AskUserQuestion) and is paused until the user resolves it. `processing` stays true while this is true.

parentChatId.description: ID of the parent chat, if this is a sub-chat

lastMessageText.description: Preview of the most recent input message sent to this chat.

EnginePreviewPort.description: A preview port forwarded from the replica

AgentEvent.description: A raw event from the coding agent, streamed as part of `chat.turn.delta` events. The shape depends on the coding agent provider. Use the `type` field to discriminate between Claude, Codex, Cursor, Opencode, and Pi events.

ClaudeAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Claude Code agent. The `type` field is prefixed with `claude-` followed by the SDK message type.

type.description: Claude event type. `claude-assistant` contains model output (text, thinking, tool use). `claude-user` contains tool results. `claude-result` signals turn completion or errors. `claude-system` contains system-level messages.

AutomationTrigger.description: A trigger that determines when an automation fires

config.description: Trigger-specific configuration. When `type` is `cron`, this is a `CronTriggerConfig`. When `type` is `github`, this is a `GitHubTriggerConfig`. When `type` is `gitlab`, this is a `GitLabTriggerConfig`. When `type` is `slack`, this is a `SlackTriggerConfig`. When `type` is `sentry`, this is a `SentryTriggerConfig`. When `type` is `custom`, this is a `CustomTriggerConfig` (empty object).

schedule.description: Cron expression (e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5" for weekdays at 9am UTC)

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the schedule (defaults to UTC)

GitHubTriggerConfig.description: Configuration for a GitHub event trigger

event.description: The GitHub event to listen for

repository_ids.description: Optional filter: only fire for events from these repositories. If omitted, fires for all repositories.

group_pr_events.description: When true, later `pull_request.opened`, `pull_request.synchronize`, or `pull_request.command` events for a PR that already has a workspace from an earlier run of this automation are routed to that workspace as a follow-up message instead of spawning a new one. Only meaningful for the opened, synchronize, and command events.

excluded_actors.description: Optional exclusion list: events sent by these GitHub usernames never fire the automation (e.g. `dependabot[bot]`). Matching is case-insensitive and ignores a leading `@`.

GitLabTriggerConfig.description: Configuration for a GitLab merge request event trigger

event.description: The GitLab event to listen for

repository_ids.description: Optional filter: only fire for events from these GitLab projects. If omitted, fires for all projects.

group_pr_events.description: When true, later `merge_request.opened` or `merge_request.updated` events for an MR that already has a workspace from an earlier run of this automation are routed to that workspace as a follow-up message instead of spawning a new one. Only meaningful for the opened and updated events.

excluded_actors.description: Optional exclusion list: events sent by these GitLab usernames never fire the automation. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores a leading `@`.

SlackTriggerConfig.description: Configuration for a Slack event trigger

event.description: The Slack event to listen for

channel_ids.description: Optional filter: only fire for events from these Slack channels. If omitted, fires for all channels.

group_thread_replies.description: When true (default), thread replies flow to the same workspace as the root message instead of spawning new ones.

SentryTriggerConfig.description: Configuration for a Sentry event trigger

event.description: The Sentry event to listen for

project_slugs.description: Optional filter: only fire for events from these Sentry project slugs. If omitted, fires for all projects.

min_level.description: Optional minimum severity level (inclusive). If omitted, fires for all levels.

CustomTriggerConfig.description: Configuration for a custom webhook trigger. The config is intentionally empty: the automation's generated `webhook_token` is the only thing that needs to be stored.

WorkspaceConfig.description: Workspace behavior configuration. Missing capabilities and preferences default to disabled.

capabilities.description: Actions this workspace is allowed to perform. Automations snapshot this config onto each workspace they create; API-created replicas can set it at creation time.

pr_followups.description: Whether matching pull requests can receive Replicas follow-up actions. Defaults to true for workspaces created from the dashboard, Slack, Linear, GitHub, or the API, and to false for workspaces created from an automation. When enabled, later CI and review-comment replies can route back to this workspace.

preferences.description: Workspace behavior preferences that do not grant new action permissions.

keep_open_on_pr_merge.description: Whether the workspace should remain open after its last tracked PR is merged. Defaults to false.

keep_open_on_pr_close.description: Whether the workspace should remain open after its last tracked PR is closed without merging. Defaults to false.

provisioning_error.description: Setup/provisioning or wake/resume failure captured when the workspace remains queryable in `error` status. Some wake/resume failures can be retried; the `error` status can also represent an unrecoverable sandbox failure.

message.description: Underlying setup failure message, such as repository clone/auth errors.

prompt.description: The instruction sent to the coding agent when the automation fires

debounce_seconds.description: Optional per-automation debounce window in seconds. Null or 0 disables debouncing.

environment_id.description: ID of the environment this automation runs in. The environment supplies the repository (or repository set) and the env vars / MCPs / skills layered on top of the org-wide Global environment.

webhook_token.description: Unique token for the automation's custom webhook. Present only when a `custom` trigger is configured. The public webhook URL is `POST /v1/automations/webhook/{webhook_token}`. Treat the token like an API key: the URL alone is enough to fire the automation.

cron_expression.description: Derived cron expression (from the cron trigger, if any)

cron_next_fire_at.description: Next scheduled fire time for cron automations

user_id.description: User ID for personal automations, null for org-owned automations

workspace_lifecycle_policy.description: Lifecycle policy for workspaces created by this automation

workspace_auto_stop_minutes.description: Inactivity timeout in minutes (3-1440) for default keep-alive and delete_after_inactivity policies

workspace_size.description: Compute size for workspaces fired off by this automation. Defaults to `small` when omitted.

model.description: Model override for this automation. Null uses the agent default.

workspace_id.description: The workspace created for this execution

ClaudeEventPayload.description: Payload of a Claude Code agent event, wrapping the Claude SDK message.

subtype.description: Present on `claude-result` events; `success` indicates a clean turn completion. Any other value (e.g. `error`) signals a failed turn even when `is_error` is false.

parent_tool_use_id.description: If this message is the result of a sub-agent tool call, the parent tool_use ID

is_error.description: Present on `claude-result` events; true if the turn ended with an error

errors.description: Array of error messages, present on `claude-result` events when `is_error` is true

ClaudeMessage.description: A Claude SDK message containing an array of content blocks.

content.description: Ordered list of content blocks produced or consumed by the model.

ClaudeContentBlock.description: A single content block within a Claude message. Discriminated by `type`.

oneOf.title: TextBlock
oneOf.description: A text response from the model.

oneOf.title: ThinkingBlock
oneOf.description: An extended-thinking block showing the model's reasoning.

oneOf.title: ToolUseBlock
oneOf.description: A tool invocation by the model (e.g. Bash, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Read, WebSearch, TaskCreate, Skill).

id.description: Unique ID for this tool use, referenced by subsequent tool_result blocks

oneOf.title: ToolResultBlock
oneOf.description: The result of a tool invocation, sent back to the model in `claude-user` events.

tool_use_id.description: ID of the tool_use block this result corresponds to

content.description: Tool output — either a plain string or an array of text/image blocks.

is_error.description: Whether the tool execution resulted in an error

CodexAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Codex CLI agent. Uses either `event_msg` for high-level messages or `response_item` for structured response items.

type.description: `event_msg` carries high-level messages (user input, reasoning). `response_item` carries structured responses (assistant messages, function calls, tool calls).

CursorAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Cursor agent. Cursor events are normalized with a `cursor-` prefixed type and a provider payload.

type.description: Cursor event type. `cursor-assistant` contains model output, `cursor-thinking` contains reasoning text, `cursor-tool_call` contains tool progress/results, `cursor-task` contains task updates, `cursor-status` contains run status, and `cursor-error` contains failure details.

payload.description: Cursor event payload. Shape depends on the parent event `type`; Cursor payload sub-shapes are not yet formally specified.

OpencodeAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Opencode agent. Opencode events are normalized with an `opencode-` prefixed type and an open provider payload.

type.description: Opencode event type. Common values include `opencode-message.updated`, `opencode-session.idle`, `opencode-error`, and `opencode-part-*` events.

payload.description: Opencode event payload. Shape depends on the parent event `type`; Opencode payload sub-shapes are not yet formally specified.

PiAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Pi coding agent. Pi events expose session lifecycle, text and reasoning updates, tool execution, and errors.

type.description: Pi event type. Common values include pi-message_update, pi-tool_execution_start, pi-tool_execution_update, pi-tool_execution_end, and pi-error.

payload.description: Pi event payload. Shape depends on the parent event type.

CodexEventPayload.description: Payload of a Codex CLI agent event. Shape depends on the parent event `type`.

CodexEventMsgPayload.description: Payload for `event_msg` events — high-level user or reasoning messages.

type.description: `user_message` for user input, `agent_reasoning` for the agent's chain-of-thought

message.description: User message text (present when type is `user_message`)

CodexResponseItemPayload.description: Payload for `response_item` events — structured items from the Codex response stream.

oneOf.title: AssistantMessage
oneOf.description: A text message from the Codex agent.

oneOf.title: FunctionCall
oneOf.description: A function call by the Codex agent (shell commands, plan updates).

call_id.description: Unique ID for this call, referenced by the corresponding `function_call_output`

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments (e.g. `{"command": "ls -la"}` for shell commands, `{"plan": [...]}` for plan updates)

oneOf.title: FunctionCallOutput
oneOf.description: Output from a previously invoked function call.

call_id.description: ID of the function_call this output corresponds to

output.description: Raw output string. For shell commands this may include exit codes and stdout/stderr.

oneOf.title: CustomToolCall
oneOf.description: A custom tool invocation (e.g. `apply_patch` for file edits).

oneOf.title: CustomToolCallOutput
oneOf.description: Output from a custom tool call.

call_id.description: ID of the custom_tool_call this output corresponds to

Environment.description: An environment — the config bundle workspaces are created from. Holds an optional repository binding plus the runtime variables, files, skills, MCPs, and warm hook applied to every workspace built from it. Every organization has a singleton Global environment (`is_global: true`) whose values are layered onto every other environment. Personal environments have `user_id` set and are visible only to their owner. Source-backed personal environments expose source-derived repository binding and system prompt values while keeping the source link in `source_environment_id`.

user_id.description: Owning user for personal environments. Null for team environments.

is_global.description: True for the org's singleton Global environment, whose values apply to every workspace. Global envs cannot be deleted, cannot be edited via PATCH, and have no repository binding.

repository_id.description: Bound repository ID. Mutually exclusive with `repository_set_id`. Both null = unbound repo-less workspace.

repository_set_id.description: Bound repository set ID. Mutually exclusive with `repository_id`.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt prepended to every workspace's coding agent.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Whether workspaces from this environment receive mobile simulator access. Available on Team and Enterprise plans and configurable only on team environments.

personal_preferences.description: User-authored instructions appended after the (inherited) system prompt. Only settable on personal environments, and editable even when source-backed.

source_environment_id.description: Source team environment for source-backed personal environments. Null for standalone personal environments and team environments.

variable_count.description: Number of variables attached to this environment

CreateEnvironmentRequest.description: Request body for creating a new environment.

name.description: Human-readable name (must be unique within the selected scope)

scope.description: `org` creates a team environment. `user` creates a personal environment visible only to the authenticated user.

source_environment_id.description: Optional source. Team environments copy from the source on create. Personal environments inherit from a team source and keep inherited config locked.

repository_id.description: Bind to this repository. Mutually exclusive with `repository_set_id`.

repository_set_id.description: Bind to this repository set. Mutually exclusive with `repository_id`.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt prepended to the coding agent.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Enable mobile testing. Only valid for team environments on Team and Enterprise plans; otherwise returns `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment. Only provided fields are changed. `repository_id` and `repository_set_id` remain mutually exclusive when both are supplied.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Enable or disable mobile testing. Only valid on team environments; enabling requires a Team or Enterprise plan and otherwise returns `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`.

personal_preferences.description: Only settable on personal environments. Appended after the (inherited) system prompt.

EnvironmentVariable.description: An environment variable. Values are encrypted at rest and decrypted on read.

personal_override_allowed.description: Whether source-backed personal environments may override this inherited key

CreateEnvironmentVariableRequest.description: Request body for creating an environment variable.

personal_override_allowed.description: Team/Global variables only. Allows source-backed personal environments to override this inherited key.

UpdateEnvironmentVariableRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment variable. Only provided fields are changed.

personal_override_allowed.description: Team/Global variables only. Allows source-backed personal environments to override this inherited key.

EnvironmentFile.description: A file dropped into the workspace at the configured `path` when the workspace is provisioned.

path.description: Destination path inside the workspace (typically under `~/`)

CreateEnvironmentFileRequest.description: Request body for creating an environment file. Maximum content size is 64 KB (65,536 bytes).

path.description: Destination path inside the workspace, e.g. `~/AGENTS.md`

UpdateEnvironmentFileRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment file. Only provided fields are changed.

EnvironmentSkill.description: A skill enabled on an environment. The membership row, not the catalog entry.

source.description: Catalog URL or other source identifier

CreateEnvironmentSkillRequest.description: Request body for enabling a skill on an environment.

name.description: Display name (typically copied from the catalog result)

source.description: Catalog URL or other source identifier

RepoSkillFramework.description: Which AI tool owns the discovered file's on-disk convention.

RepoSkill.description: A skill/agent/command/prompt file discovered inside the environment's bound repo. Distinct from `EnvironmentSkill`: these are inferred live from the repo's git tree, are read-only, and have no DB row.

id.description: Stable id, formed from the repository UUID and the in-repo path.

branch.description: Default branch the file was resolved against.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the discovered file or skill directory.

name.description: Human-friendly name (from YAML frontmatter when present, otherwise the filename or directory).

description.description: Single-line description, populated from frontmatter when available.

error.description: Populated when discovery couldn't run end-to-end (e.g. the bound repo has no GitHub App installation). The list may still be partially filled; the UI shows this as an inline banner rather than a 5xx.

EnvironmentSkillsRegistry.description: A GitHub repository registered as a skill registry on an environment.

EnvironmentSkillsRegistryWithContents.description: A skill registry with its discovered skills.

installs.description: Approximate install count from the catalog

EnvironmentMcpStdioConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP that runs a local subprocess (`transport: stdio`).

EnvironmentMcpHttpConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP reached over HTTP or SSE (`transport: http` or `transport: sse`).

EnvironmentMcpConfig.description: MCP transport-specific configuration. Discriminate by the parent `transport` field.

EnvironmentMcp.description: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server attached to an environment.

name.description: MCP name (1–64 chars, must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`; cannot start with reserved prefix `replicas-`)

CreateEnvironmentMcpRequest.description: Request body for creating an MCP. The `config` shape must match the chosen `transport`.

UpdateEnvironmentMcpRequest.description: Request body for updating an MCP. Only provided fields are changed. When `transport` is changed, `config` is required and must match the new transport's shape.

WarmHookRecord.description: A warm hook — the shell script that runs while pre-warming workspaces for an environment.

version.description: Monotonic version (newer scripts have higher versions)

is_active.description: Whether this version is the active one for the environment

WarmPoolConfigWithStats.description: Warm pool configuration plus current pool counts.

generation.description: Monotonic counter bumped on every invalidation. Workspaces and snapshots carry the generation they were built for; anything older is stale by derivation.

error_count.description: Consecutive reconcile failures since the last success. Resets to 0 on success; drives exponential backoff via `next_retry_at`.

next_retry_at.description: Earliest time the next reconcile pass may run for this config. Null when not in backoff.

last_error_at.description: When the most recent reconcile error was recorded (null if no current error).

last_error_message.description: Most recent reconcile error message (null if no current error).

has_base_snapshot.description: True when a base snapshot is installed for the current generation. For snapshot-capable providers (E2B), distinguishes the initial seed-build phase (false + warming > 0) from the clone-refill phase (true + warming > 0). Always false on providers without live snapshots.

ready_count.description: Number of pre-warmed workspaces at the current generation that are ready to be assigned

stale_count.description: Number of ready workspaces at older generations. Still claimable as a fallback; trimmed by reconcile when over target.

warming_count.description: Number of workspaces at the current generation that are currently warming (warm hooks running)

snapshotting_count.description: Number of seed workspaces currently capturing a base snapshot (E2B only). Always 0 on providers without live snapshots.

last_failure_at.description: When the most recent warm-up failure occurred (null if never)

last_failure_reason.description: Reason for the most recent warm-up failure

warm_hook.description: The active warm hook for the environment (null if none has ever been saved).

warm_pool.description: The warm pool config and current counts (null if no pool has been configured).

WarmHookTestResult.description: Result of running a warm hook script in an isolated sandbox.

timed_out.description: Whether execution was killed for taking too long

content.description: Shell script to persist and activate
Shell script to save and execute

StartHookRecord.description: A start hook — the shell script that runs at workspace boot (after the warm sandbox is claimed) for an environment.

version.description: Monotonic version (newer scripts have higher versions)

is_active.description: Whether this version is the active one for the environment

start_hook.description: The active start hook for the environment (null if none has ever been saved).

content.description: Shell script to persist and activate. Empty content clears the active start hook.

start_hook.description: The saved active start hook, or null when the request cleared the active start hook.

StartHookTestResult.description: Result of running a start hook script in an isolated sandbox.

timed_out.description: Whether execution was killed for taking too long

enabled.description: Whether the warm pool should be active

WarmPoolWorkspaceRecord.description: A single pre-warmed workspace within a warm pool.

generation.description: Config generation this workspace was built for. Less than the parent config's `generation` means stale by derivation.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID containing the thread.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace ID. Required outside agent mode.
